steps: Start a throwaway standard-library listener on 127.0.0.1 with a random bearer token; it records names only and answers every request with an empty 200.

Run one claude -p session with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:<port>, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=Authorization=Bearer <token>, and a throwaway --settings file with HTTP hooks (SessionStart, SessionEnd, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PostToolUse; header Authorization: Bearer $PROBE_TOKEN via allowedEnvVars; timeout 5).
Prompt and allowed tools as in `command`: one general-purpose subagent runs `echo probe-ok`.
Stop the listener and rerun the same session (run 2).
command: claude -p "Use the Task tool to launch one general-purpose subagent whose only job is to run the Bash command: echo probe-ok — and report its output. Then reply with exactly the subagent's reported output." --settings <throwaway-settings.json> --allowedTools "Task" "Bash(echo:*)" --model haiku
expected: OTLP JSON with token, cost, model, agent and parent-agent identifiers; tool calls unaffected by empty hook responses or a stopped listener.

listenerStopped.stderr: one line: the SessionEnd HTTP hook failed with ECONNREFUSED; no other hook error reported

checks.check: OTLP logs and metrics arrive as uncompressed JSON over HTTP with the configured authorization header
OTLP carries token, cost, model, session and prompt identifiers
OTLP carries agent and parent-agent identifiers
checks.detail: No agent_id or parent_agent_id attribute was emitted; only agent.name, agent_type, agent.source and query_source. Per-subagent attribution must come from hook payloads (agent_id, agent_type on SubagentStart, SubagentStop and PostToolUse inside a subagent), not from OpenTelemetry.

checks.check: Empty-bodied HTTP hook responses leave the tool call and the subagent unaffected
A stopped listener leaves the session unaffected

checks.detail: No SessionStart request reached the listener in run 1; the viewer cannot rely on an HTTP SessionStart hook and must open a strand from the first event it receives.

findingsForAllowlist: Privacy-relevant names are emitted even with OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS unset: prompt, prompt_text, response, user.email, user.id, user.account_id, user.account_uuid, organization.id. The OTLP allowlist must drop them.

Hook payloads carry content and paths: tool_input.command, tool_input.prompt, tool_response.stdout, tool_response.stderr, tool_response.prompt, last_assistant_message, cwd, transcript_path, agent_transcript_path, scratchpad_dir. The hook adapter must drop them.
limits: One machine, one account, one installed version; names can change between host versions.
Names only: the throwaway listener recorded field and attribute names, never values; whether privacy-relevant values were redacted by the host was not checked.
The throwaway listener (sha256 74f85b3b383c0ff1f607f9b7eea347f36227904a5a842ba0eedd178b2c19c0d8) is not committed, per the runbook.
Non-interactive claude -p only; the interactive terminal and desktop clients were not probed for OpenTelemetry or hooks.
Hooks were passed with --settings rather than a user-level settings profile; the effect on hook delivery is not assumed to differ but was not compared.
Single session per run; event ordering, batching intervals and rate limits were not measured.
The SessionStart absence was observed once under claude -p and may depend on the client mode.
Pinning the exact allowlist is a reviewed change at implementation (T016, T019); this receipt does not change plan.md.
Embedded hashes of the uncommitted throwaway listener and fixture identify the bytes used only; they are not repository-verifiable.
Sorted name lists replace raw excerpts by design (names-only probe); no payload bytes were kept.
outcomeRationale: The three ingest paths (otlp-logs, otlp-metrics, claude-hook) work, so no path is removed from VIS.1 and the row is verified. The two not-matching checks are field-level expectations: OpenTelemetry has no agent or parent-agent id (attribution moves to hook agent_id) and no HTTP SessionStart hook arrived under claude -p (a strand opens on the first event). The contract allowlist in contracts/ui-security-privacy.md still names agent_id, parent_agent_id and SessionStart; it is re-pinned through the reviewed change at T016 and T019.
